skill.name: integration-privy
skill.description: Integrate Privy authentication with Sign-In-With-Solana in Expo Android apps that use Mobile Wallet Adapter.
skill.summary: Configure Privy, implement SIWS login and linking, verify sessions, and troubleshoot Expo Android integration.
skill.author: solana-mobile

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, public Expo identifiers, documented server variables, and expected Privy network calls. The predictable temporary path is a real filesystem risk. Repeated closing content tags and unpinned npx execution require remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Two reference files contain unexplained </content> boundary tags.
remediation.suggestion: Remove both tags and review the source history for other prompt-boundary or instruction-like text before resubmission.

remediation.issue: The reference command executes the mutable solana-mobile@latest package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and checksum, and require user confirmation before downloading or executing it.

remediation.issue: The generated reference project uses a fixed shared temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique temporary directory, verify it is newly created, and state what files the command will create.

content.user_title: Integrate Privy Authentication with Solana Mobile
content.value_statement: Solana mobile apps need durable user accounts without moving signing keys into the application. This skill connects Privy sessions to MWA-based Sign-In-With-Solana.
actual_capabilities: Configure Privy public identifiers, Expo plugins, polyfills, and Metro resolution.
Mount Privy, React Query, and Mobile Wallet Adapter providers.
Implement SIWS message generation, wallet signing, and Privy login.
Link a Solana wallet to an existing Privy account.
Verify Privy access tokens on a backend with issuer and audience checks.
Diagnose initialization, encoding, dashboard, session, and peer dependency failures.
limitations: Supports Android development builds because Mobile Wallet Adapter does not support iOS or Expo Go.
Assumes a working Mobile Wallet Adapter integration already exists.
Does not manage private keys or sign transactions through Privy.
Requires developer-owned Privy credentials, dashboard configuration, and backend deployment.

use_cases.title: Add wallet authentication
use_cases.description: Build SIWS login for an Expo Android application that already connects through Mobile Wallet Adapter.

use_cases.title: Link existing accounts
use_cases.description: Attach a connected Solana wallet to a Privy user who first authenticated with email or OAuth.

use_cases.title: Secure backend sessions
use_cases.description: Validate Privy access tokens and derive trusted user identity before granting server resources.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Expo Android project and list the missing prerequisites for Privy SIWS with Mobile Wallet Adapter.

prompt_templates.title: Configure providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the required Privy, React Query, and Mobile Wallet Adapter provider configuration to my existing application structure.

prompt_templates.title: Implement SIWS
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement Privy SIWS login and wallet linking using my existing Mobile Wallet Adapter hooks and stable domain values.

prompt_templates.title: Harden token verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my client and backend Privy flow for token caching, audience validation, wallet ownership, account linking, and sign-out consistency.

output_examples.output: The review identifies missing public identifiers, provider ordering, native plugins, Metro configuration, and rebuild requirements.

output_examples.input: Why does SIWS reject my signed message?
output: Confirm SVM wallets are enabled in Privy.
Verify the Android package matches the client identifier.
Use the base58 address and preserve the complete signed payload.

output_examples.input: How should my server trust a Privy session?
output_examples.output: Verify the access token signature, algorithm, issuer, and application audience, then load wallet data from the verified user record.

best_practices: Keep the Privy app secret on the server and expose only public client identifiers.
Request a fresh access token for each backend call and validate its audience.
Clear both Privy and wallet sessions during sign-out.
anti_patterns: Do not place the Privy app secret in an EXPO_PUBLIC variable.
Do not treat a client-supplied user identifier or wallet address as verified identity.
Do not convert the signed payload to base58 or truncate it.

faq.question: Does this skill support iOS?
faq.answer: No. The described flow depends on Mobile Wallet Adapter, which is limited to Android.

faq.question: Can this run in Expo Go?
faq.answer: No. Privy and wallet dependencies require native modules in an Expo development build.

faq.question: Does Privy hold the wallet private key?
faq.answer: No. The external wallet retains keys and approves every signature through Mobile Wallet Adapter.

faq.question: Are the Expo Privy identifiers secret?
faq.answer: No. The app ID and client ID are public, but the Privy app secret must remain server-side.

faq.question: Can the skill verify backend sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Privy SDK verification and direct JWT validation with algorithm, issuer, and audience checks.

faq.question: Why must sign-out clear two sessions?
faq.answer: Privy and Mobile Wallet Adapter persist independent sessions. Clearing only one leaves authentication or wallet authorization active.
